chapter_title: Concerning the Sect of the Basket
spiritual_reading:
# Spiritual Translation

---

## ¶5

The [GAP-1] and the great [GAP-2] and the great interior perception that is [GAP-3] — this new regenerating understanding that is with the [GAP-4] — thirty-six operative divine truths [GAP-5] — twenty-two divine truths ordering the whole of intelligence [GAP-6] — but [GAP-7] of the twenty-two [GAP-8] — the seven fundamental principles of divine order that sust[GAP-9: ain] — the encompassing sphere of natural knowledge surrounding the whole mind [GAP-10] — four essential truths that are distributed throughout the [GAP-11] whole mind, upholding the power of the Divine [GAP-12] in the external and natural degree, which is the foundation upon which all interior states of wisdom rest [GAP-13] — these other five essential divine faculties, the powers proceeding from the Celestial Human, they that [GAP-14] — the whole mind is established in permanent order [GAP-15] — the calling-forth of divine truth and the will's willing reception of it [GAP-16] — the radiance of [GAP-17] — and the indestructible divine truth [GAP-18] — they have become opposing falsities from evil [GAP-19] — yet they are led by influx from within.

---

The seven principles of divine order correspond to the complete and holy foundations upon which all regeneration stands. The encompassing sphere of natural knowledge is what contains and bounds the entire mind at its outermost degree — all interior states terminate into it. The four essential truths distributed to every quarter signify completeness of divine support in every direction of the will and understanding. The five faculties proceeding from the Celestial Human are the inmost goods and truths through which the whole structure of the mind is held firm. The Calling-forth and the Reception are the two reciprocal movements of all spiritual life: the Divine speaks, and the will answers. The indestructible divine truth is that innermost certainty which cannot be shattered by any assault of falsity. Yet even among these ordered powers, some have turned into their opposites — becoming hostile to the very order they were meant to serve — and nonetheless they are governed, through permission and providence, from within.

---

## ¶6

The third degree likewise: [GAP-20] — in the lower and natural plane, there are twelve complete truths of faith standing firm in their order. However, the full number of the twelve representative forms [GAP-21] — the three great sustaining principles of divine power that [GAP-22] — fundamental truths upholding the sphere of the spiritual sun [GAP-23] — the other three [GAP-24] — these are the external truths with which the Divine Proceeding that vivifies all things [GAP-25] — it clothed the mind in those external truths at the time of its ordering [GAP-26] — that cast them forth, together with [GAP-27] — which is made manifest therein [GAP-28] — this [GAP-29] — complete and whole before [GAP-30] — the great guardian truth that watches over the threshold between states [GAP-31] — in its own power and dominion [GAP-32] — these are the three great [GAP-33] — opposing [GAP-34] — are active within the interior affections and thoughts of the human mind [GAP-35] — perceives [GAP-36] — commits the whole of one's interior life into their keeping [GAP-37].

---

The twelve truths of faith in the natural degree are the complete doctrinal form through which the Divine order reaches into outward life. The three sustaining principles of divine power are the inmost trine — love, wisdom, and use — that uphold the apparent form of the spiritual sun as it is received below. The external truths are garments: the Living Divine Proceeding clothes the regenerating mind in them so that interior states may be carried safely into the world. The great guardian truth stands at the threshold between the interior and exterior mind, exercising dominion over what may pass in and what must be kept out. These sustaining truths operate within the very midst of human affections and thoughts; and whoever perceives their origin and commits the whole of his interior life to their governance is held in order by them.

reconstructions.reconstructed_text: The [Light] and the great [Power] and the great Mind that is [in the height, and] this Youth that is with the [twelve maidens. The] thirty-six angels [and the] twenty-two angels [that order the heavens] but [the number] of the twenty-two [is this] the seven pillars that stan[d in] the sea that surrounds the universe [and the] four angels that are distributed to the [four corners of the] universe, supporting the mightiness [of the Father from] below, which is the earth of all the heavens [and also] these other five gods, the sons of the Man, they that [sustain it. And] the universe is stood firm [by them, and] the Summons and the Obedience [and also] the splendour of the [Light] and the Adamant of Light [but some among them] they are become enemies [to the light, yet] they guide it.

The third also, [that which is] below, there are twelve powers standing firm there. However, the number of the twelve images [is this] the three great pillars of mightiness that [are the] pillars supporting the disk [of the sun. And] the other three [images are these] they are the garments that the Living Spirit [put on, and] he put them at that time [upon those] that threw them, together with [the light] which is displayed therein [and] this [is made] perfect before [the face of the] great Porter [who stands] in his power [and might] these are the three great [garments] against [the darkness, that] are in the midst of people [and whoever] knows [them and] entrusts his soul to them [shall be saved].

fills.explanation: In the Kephalaia's register, "the Light" is the most fundamental divine principle and commonly opens enumerations of the cosmic hierarchy, corresponding to the good/love in Swedenborg's trine.
Completing a triad of Light, Power, and Mind — three fundamental divine principles corresponding to love, use, and wisdom — a standard Manichaean divine enumeration in the Kephalaia.
The Great Mind/Nous dwells "in the height" (the upper heavens) in Manichaean cosmology; the conjunction transitions to the next item in the enumeration, the Youth.
The Third Messenger (Youth) is standardly paired with the twelve maidens (Maiden of Light and her companions) in Manichaean cosmology; the period transitions to the next enumeration item.
Simple enumeration connector linking the thirty-six angels to the twenty-two angels in a continuous cosmological listing.

The spiritual reading says "ordering the whole of intelligence" — in Swedenborg's correspondences, "heavens" correspond to states of intelligence; the twenty-two angels order the heavens in the natural register.

The phrase "the number of the twenty-two" mirrors the identical construction in ¶6 ("the number of the twelve images"), introducing the breakdown of a group into its constituents — standard Kephalaia enumerative style.
Completes the formula "the number of the twenty-two is this:" which introduces the detailed enumeration of constituent cosmic powers, paralleling the identical formula in ¶6.
Completes "stand in" — the seven pillars stand in the cosmic sea, a standard Manichaean cosmological image of foundational structures situated within the encompassing waters.
Enumeration connector linking the cosmic sea to the four angels, continuing the listing of constituent cosmic structures within the twenty-two.

In Manichaean cosmology, the four supporting angels are distributed to the four corners of the universe, signifying completeness of divine support in every direction — matching the spiritual reading's "distributed throughout."

The spiritual reading says "power of the Divine" — "the Father" is the Kephalaia's standard designation for the Divine; "from below" specifies the four angels' position at the cosmic foundation supporting the Father's might upward.
Transitional connector continuing the enumeration from the earth/foundation description to the next group, the five gods — standard Kephalaia listing style.
The five sons of the Living Spirit sustain the cosmic structure — their defining function in Manichaean cosmology; the conjunction transitions to the summary statement about the universe's stability.
The universe is stood firm BY the five sons — they are the agents of its stability; the conjunction continues the enumeration to the next cosmic powers (the Summons and Obedience).
Enumeration connector linking the Summons and Obedience to the next cosmic entity (the splendour), continuing the listing of the twenty-two constituent powers.

"The splendour of the Light" is a standard Manichaean phrase; the spiritual reading's "radiance" confirms this as divine radiance, and "the Light" is the standard genitive complement in the Kephalaia register.

The spiritual commentary says "some have turned into their opposites" — in the Manichaean register, some cosmic powers (archonic/zodiacal) were corrupted by darkness; "but some among them" introduces this subset.

The corrupted cosmic powers became enemies specifically "to the light" (standard Manichaean formulation); "yet" introduces the concession that despite their enmity they still serve the cosmic order through divine governance.
The spiritual reading says "the third degree likewise: in the lower and natural plane" — "that which is below" is the Kephalaia's natural-register designation for the third/lowest cosmic degree.
Mirrors the identical formula in ¶5 ("the number of the twenty-two is this") — introducing the breakdown of the twelve images into their constituent groups, standard Kephalaia expository structure.
Identifies the three great pillars of mightiness AS the pillars supporting the disk — a standard Kephalaia identificatory construction linking a named group to its cosmic function.
The spiritual reading says "the sphere of the spiritual sun" — in the Manichaean natural register, the disk is the solar disk; the conjunction transitions to the next group of three.
Connects back to "the twelve images" by identifying the other three AS images, then introduces their description — mirroring the enumerative formula used throughout the chapter.
The Living Spirit "put on" (wore) his three garments when descending to organize the cosmos — a standard Manichaean motif; the conjunction transitions to his subsequent action of placing them.

The Living Spirit placed the garments upon those (archons) who had cast/thrown the light elements — in Manichaean cosmology, the archons seized and ejected light, and the Living Spirit subdued them using his vestments.
In Manichaean cosmology, the garments were cast together with the light particles mixed into the material cosmos; "the light which is displayed therein" = the trapped light visible in creation.
Simple conjunction connecting the description of the displayed light to the statement about its perfection before the Porter — continuing the same passage of cosmic description.

The spiritual reading says "complete and whole" corresponding to "perfect" — "is made perfect" describes how the cosmic arrangement achieves completion before the Porter who guards the threshold between states.
"Before the face of" is a standard Coptic/Semitic idiom meaning "in the presence of" — extremely common in the Kephalaia register for expressing proximity to a divine figure.

The spiritual reading describes the Porter as "watching over the threshold between states" — in the Kephalaia's natural register, the Porter "stands" at his post, exercising vigilant guardianship in his cosmic station.
The spiritual reading says "power and dominion" — "power and might" is the standard Kephalaia doublet expressing divine authority; "might" corresponds to "dominion" in the natural register.

The passage has been discussing the three garments of the Living Spirit; the spiritual reading's "external truths" correspond to garments (coverings/vestments) in the natural-plane vocabulary — garments that clothe and protect against darkness.
The three great garments oppose "the darkness" — the standard Manichaean adversary; "that" introduces the relative clause describing how these garments are present among humanity.
Introduces the conditional/soteriological clause — "whoever knows... and entrusts" is a standard Kephalaia formula for the person who recognizes divine powers and commits to their governance.
Simple connector: "whoever knows them and entrusts his soul" — recognizing the three garments (perceiving their divine origin) and then committing oneself to their keeping.

The standard Kephalaia soteriological conclusion — entrusting one's soul to the divine garments/powers results in salvation; the spiritual commentary's "held in order" corresponds to salvation in the natural register.
